title: Terminal-status list duplicated across migration + 2 SQL files + Gleam helper without a cross-layer sync guard
evidence:
supabase/migrations/20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql:138-140:
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_reference_call_live
    ON reference_call(application_id, ref_slot, owner_label)
    WHERE status NOT IN ('form_completed','unreachable','refused','objected','manual_recorded','failed','completed','partial');

server/src/reference_checks/sql/insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql:28-32:
  ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (
    'form_completed', 'unreachable', 'refused', 'objected',
    'manual_recorded', 'failed', 'completed', 'partial'
  )

server/src/reference_checks/sql/insert_reference_call_skipped.sql:24-28: identical NOT IN list.

server/src/reference_checks/trigger.gleam:787-798:
  fn is_terminal(status: String) -> Bool {
    list.contains(
      [
        "form_completed",
        "unreachable",
        "refused",
        "objected",
        "manual_recorded",
        "failed",
        "completed",
        "partial",
      ],
      status,
    )
  }

server/test/reference_checks/schema_migration_test.gleam:1 const migration_path = "../supabase/migrations/20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql" — its skipped_not_in_live_index_exclusion_test pins ONLY the migration index's NOT IN set; it never reads the two insert SQL files or calls is_terminal.
detail: The 8-status terminal set is hand-copied into the migration index, both ON CONFLICT predicates, and is_terminal. The existing test pins only the migration; the other three copies can drift silently, making live-slot semantics disagree across layers.
recommended_fix: Extend schema_migration_test (or a sibling) to read the two insert SQL files and assert their ON CONFLICT NOT IN set and trigger.is_terminal's output match the idx_reference_call_live predicate, so drift fails CI.
